def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    background = grid[0][0]

    # Divider positions are the regularly spaced rows/columns whose
    # values differ from the large uniform interior cells.
    def divider_positions(axis_len, get_line):
        signatures = [tuple(get_line(i)) for i in range(axis_len)]
        best = None
        for step in range(2, axis_len):
            positions = list(range(axis_len))
            groups = {}
            for i in positions:
                groups.setdefault(i % step, []).append(signatures[i])
            score = sum(sum(a == b for a, b in zip(v, v[1:])) for v in groups.values())
            if best is None or score > best[0]:
                best = (score, step)
        step = best[1] if best else 1
        return list(range(0, axis_len, step))

    # Sample points on the separator lattice. The lattice spacing is
    # identifiable from the repeated uniform bands/cell interiors.
    def runs(axis):
        n = h if axis == 0 else w

        sig = [signature(i) for i in range(n)]
        candidates = []
        for step in range(2, min(n, 10)):
            # favor spacing where sampled lines have matching appearances
            score = sum(sig[i] == sig[i-step] for i in range(step, n))
            candidates.append((score, step))
        return max(candidates)[1]

    # Separator lines are at regular intervals; sample their crossings.

    cw = 6 if w % 6 == 0 else 7

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    # Find regularly spaced separator rows and columns by looking for
    # lines that mostly contain the separator/background color.
    sep = grid[0][0]

    def line_score(axis, i):
        line = grid[i] if axis == 0 else [grid[r][i] for r in range(h)]
        return sum(v == sep for v in line) / len(line)

    def period(axis, n):
        scores = [line_score(axis, i) for i in range(n)]
        candidates = []
        for p in range(2, min(n, 10)):
            positions = list(range(0, n, p))
            candidates.append((sum(scores[i] for i in positions) / len(positions), p))
        return max(candidates)[1]

    rp, cp = period(0, h), period(1, w)
    rlines = list(range(0, h, rp))
    clines = list(range(0, w, cp))

    # A marker is any separator intersection whose color is not the
    # ordinary separator color. Keep the lattice rectangle surrounding
    # all such markers, filling ordinary intersections with the cell color.
    marked = [(i, j) for i, r in enumerate(rlines)
              for j, c in enumerate(clines) if grid[r][c] != sep]
    if not marked:
        return [[grid[1][1]]]
    r0 = min(i for i, _ in marked)
    r1 = max(i for i, _ in marked)
    c0 = min(j for _, j in marked)
    c1 = max(j for _, j in marked)
    fill = grid[1][1]
    return [[grid[rlines[i]][clines[j]] if grid[rlines[i]][clines[j]] != sep else fill
             for j in range(c0, c1 + 1)] for i in range(r0, r1 + 1)]

def transform(grid):
    h, w = len(grid), len(grid[0])
    base = grid[0][0]

    # Find the separator spacing: grid lines have a repeated base-color
    # band, while the intervening regions are uniform cell interiors.
    def spacing(n, line):
        best = None
        for p in range(2, min(10, n)):
            score = sum(line(i) == line(i - p) for i in range(p, n))
            if best is None or score > best[0]:
                best = (score, p)
        return best[1]

    rh = spacing(h, lambda i: tuple(grid[i]))
    cw = spacing(w, lambda j: tuple(grid[i][j] for i in range(h)))
    rows = list(range(0, h, rh))
    cols = list(range(0, w, cw))

    # Keep only divider lines that have at least one colored marker at
    # a crossing, then crop to the marker-bearing rectangle.
    active_rows = [r for r in rows if any(grid[r][c] != base for c in cols)]
    active_cols = [c for c in cols if any(grid[r][c] != base for r in rows)]
    if not active_rows or not active_cols:
        return [[base]]
    r0, r1 = min(active_rows), max(active_rows)
    c0, c1 = min(active_cols), max(active_cols)
    active_rows = [r for r in rows if r0 <= r <= r1 and r in active_rows]
    active_cols = [c for c in cols if c0 <= c <= c1 and c in active_cols]
    return [[grid[r][c] for c in active_cols] for r in active_rows]

def transform(grid):

    # six columns. Return the junction-color pattern, replacing ordinary
